messages:
Maria G: Heads-up — post-incident notes from the APAC holiday surge (near-OOM / throttling). Quick summary: sudden 3.2x sustained traffic spike starting ~2026-03-14 02:10 UTC, autoscaler reacted late, KV cache churn increased GPU memory pressure, some LBs hit AZ egress quotas and we saw token throttling on a subset of Dedicated pools. Not a total outage but a near-miss we should capture.

Kevin T: thanks, Maria. do we have a short timeline + root cause hypotheses?

Maria G: timeline in one line: external promo kicked at 02:08, traffic ramped 02:09–02:15, first token retries at 02:12, autoscaler started scale-up 02:18, effective new capacity 02:27. Hypotheses: (1) forecast underpredicted holiday uplift in APAC region, (2) autoscaler scale-up thresholds + cooldown too conservative, (3) KV cache eviction amplified per-request cold-start memory, (4) AZ egress quotas caused uneven routing -> hotspots.

Anna SRE: Adding logs snippet we looked at: 
```
[2026-03-14 02:12:07] pool-ded-APAC-1: free_gpu_mem_percent=7.3, kv_cache_evictions=1290/min
[2026-03-14 02:13:01] routing: 14% requests->fallback-region(euw1) due_to:az_egress_quota
[2026-03-14 02:14:45] token_throttle: 503 throttle_rate=0.04 backlog=312
```

Devon (infra): the autoscaler config we had was intentionally conservative for cost reasons. current config: 
```
autoscaler:
  scale_up_delay: 90s
  scale_up_step: 1
  max_scale_per_minute: 2
  min_idle_gpus: 1
```
That combined with a 30s sampling window meant we didn't breach thresholds until the backlog already climbed.

Lia: were any dedicated pools pinned to model variants with higher mem profiles? I remember a canary pushed a larger variant last week.

Kevin T: yes — two canary groups were serving a v2-large quant profile (higher KV working set). Those groups accounted for ~18% of started sessions in APAC slice.

Anna SRE: Another nuance: egress quotas in ap-east-1 AZ-b caused some of our router nodes to shift traffic to fewer AZs, increasing localized memory pressure. We saw per-AZ GPU util jump to 98% while cluster-wide average was 75%.

Maria G: Cost note: overnight committed pool utilization hit 92% which is high but fine. The problem was underprovisioned planned headroom for a holiday uplift scenario — forecast model used seasonal multiplier 1.4 but real uplift was 3.2. Forecast inputs missed partner promo calendar.

Devon (infra): Actionable fixes I propose: (A) short-term: bump min_idle_gpus by +20% for APAC holiday windows, relax scale_up_delay to 30s for burst policies, temporary emergency quota to allow cross-AZ egress fallback. (B) medium: add promo calendar as forecast input, add model-tag awareness to autoscaler (don't scale down groups pinned to high-mem variants). (C) long: predictive warm pool that preloads KV caches for top N models during known events.

Lia: +1 to warm pool. also we should autoscale by expected GPU memory, not just instance count. that would avoid scenarios where many small requests cause memory churn.

Kevin T: we also need to update runbook play: earlier detection metric = backlog per-GPU + kv_eviction_rate > 200/min should trigger SOS alert and preemptive scale. can someone draft a runbook change?

Anna SRE: I'll draft the runbook and add the new play: pre-scale, change routing to regional fallback, and escalate to infra within 5 minutes.

Maria G: For postmortem: root causes = forecasting gap (missed calendar), autoscaler tuning conservative for cost, KV cache eviction + model variant mix, AZ egress-induced hotspot. Impact: ~6% increased latency for some customers, a small % of requests retried, no long-duration 5xx outage.

Devon (infra): Cost tradeoffs we discussed in the incident channel: temporary increased committed capacity for peak windows will raise costs ~12% for Q2 but reduces retry/latency penalties and potential SLA credits. ops-biz, we should price this vs. customer experience.

Kevin T: I can run a quick cost-impact calc if we choose +20% committed GPUs in APAC for 2 weeks.

Maria G: please do. Action items (quick):
- Kevin: cost calc & suggestion for committed hours (due EOD)
- Anna: runbook draft with new detection and play (due EOD +1)
- Devon: prototype autoscaler change (scale_up_delay->30s, mem-aware scaling) on staging (due +3 days)
- Lia: design doc for warm pool + KV preload (due +1 week)

ops-bot: Incident tag updated: severity=SEV2, owners=[Maria G, Anna SRE, Devon (infra)] :white_check_mark:

Lia: small note — let's also add a quick test harness that simulates an APAC AZ egress quota enforcement to see routing fallback behavior.

Anna SRE: good call. I'll add that to the runbook tests.

Maria G: thanks everyone. I'll assemble a short postmortem doc and link here when ready. please keep comments inline and short. :thumbsup:
